mcp.tool.smartsearch.desc: General-purpose web search for real-time information (news, technical docs, products, data). Keep the query focused and precise; piling up synonyms and secondary terms into a keyword list dilutes relevance.
mcp.tool.smartsearch.intent: Use the intent parameter to describe the goal of the search and get a more precise structured summary.
mcp.tool.smartsearch.fetch: Use fetch_top_n to fetch the full text of the top N scored results (default 0 = no fetch, max 5).
mcp.tool.smartsearch.fallback: Falls back to Bing when the primary engine is unavailable.
mcp.tool.smartsearch.scope: Scope: time-sensitive facts, web leads and document lookup; for systematic literature reviews or academic questions that need citations, use academicsearch instead.
mcp.tool.academicsearch.desc: Academic paper search: queries several scholarly databases in parallel and returns standardized Markdown results (title, authors, DOI, venue, citation count, PDF link).
mcp.tool.academicsearch.engines: Available engines (the engines parameter accepts several; empty means all):
mcp.tool.academicsearch.advice: Engine guidance: medicine/biology → pubmed, europepmc | CS/AI → arxiv, semantic_scholar, dblp | all fields → crossref, openalex, google_scholar | open access → doaj
mcp.tool.academicsearch.doi: When you already have a DOI or arXiv id, pass it directly as query (e.g. '10.1038/s41586-020-2649-2', 'doi:10.1038/s41586-020-2649-2', 'https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2649-2' or '2401.04085', 'arXiv:2401.04085', 'https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.04085'); this performs an exact single-paper lookup (still honoring registered or explicitly requested engines; time_range and page do not apply). Given a pdf_url in the result, pass that URL as the path parameter of the pdf_parser tool to parse the full text.
mcp.tool.academicsearch.scope: Scope: papers, preprints and DOI-level scholarly lookup; for news, product docs and other general web information use smartsearch instead.
mcp.tool.academicsearch.engine.crossref: Crossref scholarly metadata (all fields, with DOI/citations)
mcp.tool.academicsearch.engine.openalex: OpenAlex open scholarly graph (all fields, with citation counts/relevance score)
mcp.tool.academicsearch.engine.semantic_: Semantic Scholar (CS/AI, with citation counts/relevance score)
mcp.tool.academicsearch.engine.google_sc: Google Scholar (all fields, with citation counts/PDF)
mcp.tool.academicsearch.engine.europepmc: Europe PMC biomedical/life sciences (PubMed supplement, with citation counts)
mcp.tool.academicsearch.engine.dblp: DBLP computer science literature (CS conference/journal index)
mcp.tool.academicsearch.engine.doaj: DOAJ open access journals (open access papers across all fields)
mcp.tool.cleanfetch.desc: Full-text retrieval tool. url/urls fetch web pages as Markdown (merged and deduplicated, up to 5); alternatively pass a result_ref returned by another tool to read saved search, web or PDF text in segments, returning content, next_offset and eof without re-requesting the source. The two modes are mutually exclusive; offset/limit apply only to reference reads. Always registered; cleanfetch.enabled controls URL fetching only. Use smartsearch first to discover sources.
mcp.tool.file_search.desc: Fast local file search backed by the Everything index, returning file names and paths in milliseconds (read-only, never reads file contents). Useful for locating local files: source code, documents, PDFs. query accepts Everything syntax (wildcards, ext:, dm:, size: and so on).
mcp.tool.file_search.roots: Search is limited to {{.RootCount}} allowlisted directories; use the folder parameter to narrow it to one of them.
mcp.tool.file_search.time: Timestamp format is selectable via time_format: datetime (default, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS) / iso / filetime.
mcp.tool.file_search.paging: 10 results per page by default (max_results is adjustable, hard cap 20); page through large result sets instead of raising max_results.
mcp.tool.pdf_parser.desc: PDF parsing tool. path is a local path visible to the service process, a file:// URI, or a remote http(s) PDF URL (a pdf_url from academic results can be passed directly). Docker can only read container or mounted paths, so file_search host paths do not carry over. Local text extraction is preferred and the response names the parser actually used; for long documents pass pages (e.g. '1-10'), otherwise only the first 20 pages (pdf_parser.max_pages) are parsed with a truncation notice; large documents can be stored to a temporary file.
mcp.tool.pdf_parser.ocr: Falls back to MinerU OCR when no local text can be extracted (scanned or image-only PDFs).
mcp.tool.pdf_parser.remote: Remote URLs matching the PDF address rules are parsed by MinerU precise mode first.
mcp.tool.pdf_parser.crop: When the original exceeds the page limit or the source URL is rejected by MinerU, the selected pages are cropped locally and uploaded in batches, with live batch progress.
mcp.tool.pdf_parser.wait: MinerU waiting time is adjustable via wait_seconds (0-1800 s, 300 s per task by default); when a task_ref is returned, omit path/pages to query the original task, which is polled once and never resubmitted.
mcp.tool.pdf_parser.scope: Scope: PDF only; for fetching web page text use cleanfetch.
mcp.tool.search_history.desc: Local search history tool (experimental, usefulness still under evaluation; FTS5 full-text matching over past queries and result titles/snippets). Omit query to list recent history in reverse chronological order.
mcp.tool.search_history.use: Suited to "what did I look up earlier" and to reusing earlier results without searching the web again; use cleanfetch on the URL when you need the full text.
mcp.tool.search_history.privacy: Data stays in a local SQLite database and never leaves the machine; written automatically after every successful smartsearch (retention defaults to 30 days).
mcp.resource.capabilities.desc: Server capability matrix: registered tools, web engines, API providers (key counts only) and feature switches (read-only, contains no secrets).
mcp.resource.health.desc: Runtime health: engine cooldowns/circuit breaking (persisted across processes) and process uptime (JSON, contains no secrets).
mcp.cap.tool.smartsearch: - `smartsearch`: general web search with concurrent multi-engine orchestration and a failure list; supports intent summaries and fetch_top_n full-text fetching
mcp.cap.tool.cleanfetch: - `cleanfetch`: reading saved content via result_ref is always available; URL fetching enabled: {{.Enabled}} (SSRF guarded, batch capable)
mcp.cap.tool.pdf_parser: - `pdf_parser`: PDF parsing (local libraries plus MinerU fallback)
mcp.cap.engines_head: ## Web engines (config switches; not a statement of reachability)
mcp.cap.engine.baidu_web: - baidu_web: {{.Enabled}} (off by default; measured as CAPTCHA-blocked)
mcp.cap.engine.googlenews: - googlenews: {{.Enabled}} (requires a proxy; redirect links resolve back to the publisher)
mcp.cap.engine.google: - google: {{.Enabled}} (off by default; the JS challenge cannot be bypassed by spoofing)
mcp.cap.providers_head: ## API providers (configured key counts; values are never echoed)
mcp.cap.feature.fetch_top_n: - fetch_top_n default: {{.Default}} (0 = titles and snippets only; an explicit agent argument wins)
mcp.cap.feature.engine_health: - Engine cooldown persistence: engine_health.json (alongside the cache database; cooldowns survive restarts to avoid immediately retrying dead engines)
mcp.param.project: Optional project statistics label: fill in only a project short name already established in the current context (Chinese is supported); omit it when unknown, do not send paths, do not guess from the query, and do not ask the user for it. Used for statistics only; it does not affect search or fetch.
mcp.param.search.query: Search keywords: express the core intent precisely and concisely (2-6 keywords or one short phrase recommended), keeping only the terms that best pin down the target. Do not pile synonyms, process words and modifiers into a keyword list, which dilutes relevance. For example use 'Go generics performance' rather than 'Go generics type parameters compile runtime performance benchmark comparison optimization usage'.
mcp.param.search.time_range: Search time range in months, limiting results to the last N months. For example 1 = last month, 3 = last 3 months, 6 = last 6 months, 12 = last year. Defaults to 3; 0 means no limit.
mcp.param.search.fetch_top_n: Full-text fetch mode: when omitted, behavior matches older versions and only engine/provider-supplied content is returned (the server-side smartsearch.fetch_top_n can change the default, which is 0 = no fetch). 0 returns titles, snippets and URLs only; 1-5 fetches the page text of the top N results — API engines that accept full text take a fast path, other engines fetch the page internally. Results blocked by anti-bot protection (JS challenge/WAF) are annotated.
mcp.param.search.intent: Search intent: describe what you want to solve or learn. For example 'how goroutine scheduling works', 'compare the React and Vue ecosystems', 'find usage examples for an API'. Providing intent yields a more precise structured summary.
mcp.param.academic.query: Academic search keywords, for example 'transformer attention mechanism' or 'CRISPR gene editing'
mcp.param.academic.engines: Specify a subset of engines (empty uses every enabled engine). Examples: ["pubmed"] for medical papers, ["arxiv"] for CS preprints, ["arxiv","crossref"] for physics/math
mcp.param.academic.time_range: Time range filter. Options: year (last year), month (last month), week (last week), day (last day). Empty means no limit
mcp.param.academic.page: Result page number (default 1); roughly 10 results per page
mcp.param.cleanfetch.url: Web page URL to fetch, for example 'https://example.com/article'; cannot be combined with result_ref
mcp.param.cleanfetch.urls: Optional batch fetch: merged and deduplicated with url, up to 5. Each URL is pre-checked and fetched independently, one failure does not affect the others, and results are returned in per-URL sections
mcp.param.cleanfetch.result_ref: Read content already saved by this service; only accepts a result_ref returned by another tool, never a path or URL; mutually exclusive with url/urls
mcp.param.cleanfetch.offset: Only for result_ref: 0-based Unicode character offset; use next_offset to continue reading
mcp.param.cleanfetch.limit: Only for result_ref: characters per segment; omitted or 0 means 4096, max 8192
mcp.param.result.ref: result_ref returned by the service; file paths and URLs are not accepted
mcp.param.result.offset: 0-based Unicode character offset; use next_offset to continue reading
mcp.param.result.limit: Maximum characters for this segment; omitted or 0 means 4096, max 8192
mcp.param.filesearch.query: Search terms, supporting Everything syntax: 'factory', '*.go', 'ext:pdf report', 'dm:lastweek', 'size:>1mb'. Do not add a '**/' prefix — the folder parameter already scopes the search; use match_regex for regular expressions
mcp.param.filesearch.folder: Restrict the search to one directory; accepts Windows (D:\CODE\ai) or Git Bash (/d/code/ai) style paths. When an allowlist is configured the path must fall inside it; omitted, every allowlisted directory is searched (with no allowlist, the whole index is searched)
mcp.param.filesearch.match_regex: Treat query as a regular expression (joined as a regex: function without affecting the directory scope; e.g. '^factory')
mcp.param.filesearch.max_results: Results per page (default 10, hard cap 20). Lower it as needed to save context; use page to page through more results, since raising this above 20 is clamped
mcp.param.filesearch.page: Page number (default 1, cap 100); the page size is set by max_results. Paging slices the post-filtered result set continuously, with no repeats or gaps between pages
mcp.param.filesearch.sort: Sort field: name (default) / date_modified / size / path. Use date_modified together with descending to find recent changes
mcp.param.filesearch.descending: Whether to sort descending (used with sort)
mcp.param.filesearch.exclude: Exclusions (array of strings, each an Everything NOT term): e.g. ["\obj\", "\node_modules\"], "old backup". Matched literally against path segments or file names; keep the leading and trailing backslashes so files whose names merely contain the word are not caught
mcp.param.filesearch.min_alignment: Vocabulary alignment threshold (0-1): results whose alignment between the query terms and the file name plus path falls below it are dropped. Overrides the server-side everything.min_alignment; 0 = rerank only, no filtering. Start at 0.3 when results are too many
mcp.param.filesearch.time_format: Timestamp format: datetime (default, 2026-01-02 15:04:05) / iso (ISO 8601 UTC) / filetime (raw Windows FILETIME)
mcp.param.pdf.path: Required for a new parse task: an absolute local PDF path visible to the service process (or file://), or a remote http(s) PDF URL. In Docker only container or mounted paths can be read, so host paths returned by file_search do not carry over. A pdf_url from academic results can be passed directly; omit when querying an existing task_ref
mcp.param.pdf.pages: Optional page range (1-based), e.g. '1-10', '1,3,5-7'. Omitted, only the first max_pages pages are parsed (20 by default) and long documents report truncation
mcp.param.pdf.task_ref: Task reference returned by MinerU: standard:<task_id>, batch:<batch_id> or agent:<task_id>. Queries or retrieves the original task without creating a new one; mutually exclusive with path/pages. Polled once by default, returning status and the reference while it is still processing
mcp.param.pdf.wait_seconds: MinerU polling wait in seconds per task, 0-1800. New parses default to 300 s, task_ref to 0 (single poll); on timeout the reference is kept for later queries, which does not mean upstream parsing failed
mcp.param.history.query: Keywords to search your own past searches (FTS5 full-text matching over queries and result titles/snippets); omitted or empty = most recent history, newest first
mcp.param.history.limit: Maximum number of history entries to return (default 10, hard cap 50)
